For the first time since the budget negotiations began last year, EU regional spending, known as cohesion policy, is a target for reductions. The European Council president proposed reducing it by €8 billion compared with the last proposal, while farmers’ subsidies remained untouched. This is a major setback for a coalition of 17 countries from Eastern and Southern Europe — including Poland, Italy and Spain — who rejected potential cuts to cohesion policy only a few days ago.
